# `allocation-after-init`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: disciplined · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports direct allocation in a function outside recognized `init*`, `create*`,
and `main` paths.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Projects that allocate at startup make out-of-memory a bounded initialization
failure instead of an arbitrary runtime failure.

## When it fires

Only allocator-typed or allocator-named direct receivers are reported;
unresolved transitive calls are silent. Functions named `init*` or `create*`
and `main`, which sets the program up, count as initialization. Like the other
disciplined-profile rules it skips `test` blocks, private functions only tests
call, and test, fuzz, and script files.

Scratch memory that a `defer` frees before the function returns is reported
too, because TigerStyle forbids memory being "dynamically allocated (or freed
and reallocated) after initialization" and such an allocation can still fail at
run time; its message says it is scratch, whose remedy is a buffer reserved
during initialization and reused. An allocation through an arena the function
receives is reported for the same reason: the arena grows after
initialization, and the rule cannot see whether a fixed buffer backs it.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn grow(gpa: std.mem.Allocator) ![]u8 {
    return try gpa.alloc(u8, 16);
}
```
